feature: Track Select Forward (A) on the timeline
summary: Premiere's A: pick a clip and everything after it on every track, then drag the lot to open or close a gap, as one undo step. Dragging any clip that is one of several picked now carries all of them, with Select too.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording, drop a second clip after it on V1 and a sound a little later.

try.do: Click the timeline once so it holds the keyboard, then press A.
Click the second clip: it and the sound after it light up, the first clip does not.
Drag that clip right about two seconds and let go.
Press Command Z once: both clips go back.
Shift-click the second clip: only the clips on its own track are picked.
Click the first clip with A to pick everything, press V, then drag any picked clip.
Right-click any clip and choose Select Forward.

evaluate: Does the third button between Select and the Blade read as a tool you would reach for, or is A enough?
Is the icon (a box with an arrow pointing right) recognisable as select forward?
When several clips are picked, is it right that dragging one moves them all even with the Select arrow?
Is Select Forward worth a row in the clip's right-click menu?
rough: The mock's timeline bar draws only Select and the Blade. The third button goes beyond it, the same size and face as the other two.
Shift-click keeps the pick to one track, the way Premiere does it. Premiere's Shift-A (Track Select Backward) is not here.
Several picked clips slide in time only: carrying them up or down onto another track does nothing, where one clip can change track.
Only the clip in your hand catches on the playhead and other edges while you drag. The other picked clips do not.
The walk presses and drags through the same code the clip's press runs, not with a posted mouse drag, because posted drags on the timeline are not reaching clips (filed separately).
